nodes.name: Pipeline Failure
nodes.notes: Fires for any workflow naming this one as its error workflow.

parameters.query:
-- Persist the failure. Stage 3 stops at recording it; Slack and escalation
-- are Stage 10's job, and they will read this table rather than replace it.
--
-- The full trigger payload goes into context as JSONB because the shape of an
-- n8n error object is not ours to control and changes between versions.
INSERT INTO salesops.pipeline_errors
    (workflow_id, workflow_name, execution_id, node_name,
     error_message, error_stack, context)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7::jsonb)
RETURNING error_id, occurred_at, workflow_name, node_name;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $json.workflow?.id ?? null, $json.workflow?.name ?? 'unknown workflow', $json.execution?.id ?? null, $json.execution?.lastNodeExecuted ?? null, $json.execution?.error?.message ?? 'unknown error', $json.execution?.error?.stack ?? null, JSON.stringify($json) ] }}

nodes.name: Fail Ingestion Run

parameters.query:
-- Close out the ingestion run this execution belongs to.
--
-- Matching on n8n_execution_id is why that column exists: without it a crashed
-- run would sit at 'running' forever and every later run would recompute its
-- window from a stale successful one.
--
-- Guarded on status = 'running' so a run that already finished is never
-- retro-actively marked failed. Zero rows updated is a valid outcome - the
-- failure may have happened before the run row was created.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs
SET status        = 'failed',
    finished_at   = now(),
    error_message = COALESCE($2, 'unknown error')
WHERE n8n_execution_id = $1
  AND status = 'running'
RETURNING run_id, batch_id::text AS batch_id, status, error_message;

nodes.notes: Flips the matching ingestion_runs row from 'running' to 'failed'.
